title: An application of separable-state nonrepresentability to Grassmann orbitopes and calibrations
description:
An application of Fawzi’s established finite-semidefinite-lift obstruction for normalized complex separable states to the oriented real Grassmann orbitope C(4,12), the mass ball in the fourth exterior power of R12. Two affine hyperplanes select a section real-linearly isomorphic to Sep(3,3). Thus this mass ball admits no finite projected semidefinite lift of any size. A compact first-moment argument refutes the universal degree-at-most-one supporting sum-of-squares assertion in Sanyal’s Oberwolfach Report13/2015, pp.708–709, in joint work with Rostalski. It gives a negative answer in general to Harvey–Lawson Question6.5: some constant closed comass-one four-form on R12 has no pointwise or local norm completion.

The conclusion is existential. A failing unnormalized functional with rational coefficients exists, but no explicit coefficient list, exact comass, rational normalized calibration, least dimension or low-dimensional classification is supplied. Classical Wirtinger/Kähler faces, established fermionic projector bodies, Vrana–Lévay’s tensor-to-wedge decomposability lemma, theta-body/moment and lift frameworks, and the earlier Sanyal–Rostalski equivalence are credited. The decisive no-lift theorem is Fawzi’s, public in2019 and published in2021; it is not reproved. Nearby quadratic Grassmann cones and unprojected-LMI obstructions have distinct embeddings or conclusions. A bounded84-query/25-primary-PDF priority comparison found no full target predecessor in inspected bodies; worldwide priority and current worldwide openness remain unestablished.

The deposit includes the proof, TeX source, scope/priority supplement, authored independent adversarial audits and portable exact symbolic arithmetic verification (Python3.10 or later, standard library only). Coordinate identities and defective-certificate controls corroborate the elementary bridge; finite checks do not replace the written proof or Fawzi’s theorem. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, source auditing and preparation. This is an unrefereed preprint with AI adversarial reviews; conventional human peer review, journal acceptance and formal proof-assistant certification are not claimed.
